title: Ensure system wide crypto policy disables macs less than 128 bits
objective: Remediate CIS checkpoint 1.6.4: Ensure system wide crypto policy disables macs less than 128 bits

playbook_input.description: Parameters the caller provides before execution

steps.name: Apply prerequisite check for crypto-policies tools
steps.function: 1. Apply prerequisite check for crypto-policies tools using command: `command -v update-crypto-policies && command -v reboot`. Expected result: both commands return paths without error.

steps.name: Create or edit the subpolicy file /etc/crypto-policies/policies/modules/NO-WEAKMAC.pmod with content disabling weak MACs
steps.function: 2. Create or edit the subpolicy file /etc/crypto-policies/policies/modules/NO-WEAKMAC.pmod with content disabling weak MACs using command: `printf '%s\n' '# This is a subpolicy to disable weak macs' 'mac = -*-64' >> /etc/crypto-policies/policies/modules/NO-WEAKMAC.pmod`. Expected result: file is created or appended with the specified lines.

steps.name: Apply the system-wide crypto policy with the NO-WEAKMAC subpolicy
steps.function: 3. Apply the system-wide crypto policy with the NO-WEAKMAC subpolicy using command: `update-crypto-policies --set DEFAULT:NO-WEAKMAC`. Expected result: command completes successfully and updates the system crypto policy.

steps.name: Reboot the system to make cryptographic settings effective for running services
steps.function: 4. Reboot the system to make cryptographic settings effective for running services using command: `reboot`. Expected result: system reboots successfully.

steps.name: Verify that MACs less than 128 bits are disabled in the active crypto policy
steps.function: 5. Verify that MACs less than 128 bits are disabled in the active crypto policy using command: `update-crypto-policies --show`. Expected result: output includes 'DEFAULT:NO-WEAKMAC' or equivalent showing the subpolicy is applied.

reference_procedure:
Note:
• The commands below are written for the included DEFAULT system-wide crypto policy. If another policy is in use and follows local site policy, replace DEFAULT with the name of your system-wide crypto policy.
• Multiple subpolicies may be assigned to a policy as a colon separated list. e.g.
DEFAULT:NO-SHA1:NO-SSHCBC
• Subpolicies:
o Not included in the update-crypto-policies --set command will not be applied to the system wide crypto policy.
o must exist before they can be applied to the system wide crypto policy.
o .pmod file filenames must be in all upper case, upper case, e.g. NO-WEAKMAC.pmod, or they will not be read by the update-crypto-policies
--set command.
Create or edit a file in /etc/crypto-policies/policies/modules/ ending in .pmod and add or modify one of the following lines:
mac = -*-64* # Disables weak macs
Example:
# printf '%s\n' "# This is a subpolicy to disable weak macs" "mac = -*-64" >> /etc/crypto-policies/policies/modules/NO-WEAKMAC.pmod
Run the following command to update the system-wide cryptographic policy
# update-crypto-policies --set
<CRYPTO_POLICY>:<CRYPTO_SUBPOLICY1>:<CRYPTO_SUBPOLICY2>:<CRYPTO_SUBPOLICY3>
Example:
update-crypto-policies --set DEFAULT:NO-SHA1:NO-WEAKMAC
Run the following command to reboot the system to make your cryptographic settings effective for already running services and applications:
# reboot
